newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-Bullish Dow boosts shares, dollar stronger.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Bullish Dow boosts shares, dollar stronger.

text.p: A bullish performance on Wall Street boosted European bourses on Tuesday, lifting London blue chips to a record high, and the dollar scaled a two-month peak against the mark.
Leading shares in London, Frankfurt and Paris all got a leg-up after the Dow Jones industrial average posted its biggest one-day gain in over a month to close 1.3 percent up.

London's blue-chip FTSE 100 index jumped 20.1 points to a record 3,930.9, surpassing its previous record of 3,922.1 set on August 28. On Monday it closed up 17.8 at 3,910.8 -- just short of its record closing high of 3,918.7, also set on August 28.
Traders said the market could hold on to its early gains through the rest of the session, as fears over U.S. interest prospects abated, boosting U.S. markets.
Some chart analysts said they believed the FTSE was set in a solid bullish pattern that will carry it to further record highs in coming sessions.

Yet Tuesday's gains were held in check by a lacklustre performance by government bonds, overshadowed by worries that Britain will cut interest rates further to stoke pre-election growth regardless of the inflation risk.
Stock and currency markets remained gripped by interest rate prospects following last Friday's U.S. jobs data showing lower unemployment and stronger earnings.

U.S. producer and consumer price data -- due Thursday and Friday -- will be scrutinised for fresh signs of inflation pressures. Many traders and investors are betting on a rise of 0.25 percentage point in U.S. interest rates when the Federal Open Market Committee next meets on September 24.
Opinions are mixed as to whether the central bank will decide this time to raise or leave interest rates unchanged, perhaps until after the November 5 presidential election.
In early European trading, the dollar sneaked above 1.50 marks, described by analysts as a big psychological barrier, to its highest level since July 16.

It firmed overnight following comments by a key Bundesbank council member that there was room for further rate cuts in Germany if M3 money growth continued to slow. Earlier Bundesbank President Has Tietmeyer said central bank governors in Basle had agreed a strong dollar was "in the interests of all".
This, together with a strong performance on Wall Street and in U.S. Treasuries, added up to a rising dollar.
In Frankfurt, German shares started well ahead, cheered by Wall Street and the firmer dollar. Dealers said sentiment was bullish and there was good potential for the market to go higher still.
The same motors, plus gains in the French franc, propelled Paris shares, which started firmer and quickly strengthened. The main CAC-40 index was almost one percentage point higher by 0930 GMT.
CURRENCIES AT 0930 GMT
The dollar was at 1.5020 marks and 109.35 yen compared with late European levels on Monday of 1.4935 and 109.15.
STOCK MARKETS AT 0930 GMT
London's FTSE 100 index was up 19.1 at 3,929.9.
Frankfurt's DAX index was up 15.48 at 2,564.21.
The Paris CAC-40 was up 17.29 at 2,037.59.
PRECIOUS METALS

Gold was fixed at its lowest level since July 9 after a sell-off on Monday pushed prices below a key support level. Bullion fixed at $382.45 an ounce, compared with Monday's afternoon fix of $384.60 and close of $383.45. Silver was also easier at 507 cents.
